fluid_statics.density_relations.title: Specific weight and specific gravity from density
assumptions: Specific gravity is relative to the stated reference density (usually water, 1000 kg/m³).

fluid_statics.viscosity_relations.title: Kinematic and dynamic viscosity (ν = μ/ρ)
assumptions: Newtonian fluid at the state point; 1 mm²/s = 1 cSt.

fluid_statics.capillary_rise.title: Capillary rise in a tube (h = 2σ cosθ/(ρgr))

variables.name: h
variables.desc: capillary rise (negative for a non-wetting liquid)

assumptions: Circular tube, contact angle θ measured through the liquid; θ > 90° (non-wetting, e.g. mercury in glass) gives a depression (h < 0). θ = 0 is perfect wetting.
method_references: Capillary rise from the Young–Laplace balance

fluid_statics.bulk_modulus_sound.title: Bulk modulus, compressibility and speed of sound (c = √(E_v/ρ))
assumptions: Small pressure perturbation (acoustic/sonic approximation). β = 1/E_v is the compressibility at the entered modulus. The speed of sound c = √(E_v/ρ) uses the isentropic (adiabatic) bulk modulus: liquids have E_s ≈ E_T so one value serves both, while for gases E_s = γp (γ = specific-heat ratio) and E_s must be entered for sonic work.

fluid_statics.hydrostatic_pressure.title: Hydrostatic pressure: gauge and absolute

variables.name: p_atm
variables.desc: atmospheric pressure at the free surface

assumptions: Incompressible fluid at rest; h measured down from the free surface; constant density.

fluid_statics.manometer.title: Manometer pressure difference (Δp = (ρ_m − ρ_f) g h)

variables.name: rho_f
variables.desc: line fluid density (0 for a gas)

assumptions: U-tube manometer with a heavier gauge fluid; the line fluid (ρ_f) fills the connecting legs above the gauge fluid (ρ_f ≈ 0 for a gas). dp is the difference across the column.
method_references: Manometer relation Δp = (ρ_m − ρ_f) g h

fluid_statics.hydrostatic_force_plane.title: Hydrostatic force and centre of pressure on an inclined plane surface

variables.name: y_cp
variables.desc: centre of pressure, measured from the surface along the plane

variables.name: y_c
variables.desc: centroid distance from the free surface along the plane

variables.name: h_c
variables.desc: vertical depth of the centroid below the free surface

variables.name: I_c
variables.desc: centroidal second moment of area about the horizontal centroidal axis

variables.name: theta
variables.desc: angle of the plane with the horizontal
variables.label: θ

assumptions: Resultant acts normal to the plane at y_cp (always below the centroid, since I_c > 0).
The centroidal second moment I_c about the axis parallel to the free surface is a user input (the section-properties section owns the shape formulas).
θ > 0 is required: a horizontal plate (θ = 0) has uniform pressure acting at the centroid, and y_c = h_c/sin θ is undefined there, so a horizontal plate must be handled separately.
method_references: F = ρg h_c A; y_cp = y_c + I_c/(A y_c)

fluid_statics.buoyancy.title: Buoyant force (Archimedes)
assumptions: Fluid at rest; V is the volume of displaced fluid (submerged volume for a floating body).

fluid_statics.metacentric_height.title: Metacentric height of a floating body (GM = KB + BM − KG)

variables.name: I
variables.desc: second moment of the waterplane area

variables.name: KB
variables.desc: height of the centre of buoyancy above the keel

variables.name: KG
variables.desc: height of the centre of gravity above the keel

assumptions: Small-angle stability of a floating body; I is the second moment of the waterplane area about the axis of tilt (section-properties section owns the shape formula). KB and KG are measured up from the keel, so GM = KM − KG = (KB + BM) − KG; GM > 0 is stable.
method_references: BM = I/V_sub; GM = KB + BM − KG

fluid_statics.rigid_body_accel.title: Rigid-body motion: uniformly accelerating fluid tank

variables.name: theta
variables.desc: angle of the free-surface normal from vertical, toward +x
variables.label: θ

variables.name: x
variables.desc: horizontal position of the point relative to the reference

variables.name: z
variables.desc: vertical position of the point relative to the reference (up positive)

assumptions: Fluid moves as a rigid body under constant acceleration (no relative motion). The free surface is a plane normal to the pressure gradient; it rises toward −x when a_x > 0. Requires g + a_z > 0; g + a_z ≤ 0 (free fall) raises an error.

fluid_statics.rigid_body_rotation.title: Rigid-body motion: rotating fluid container (forced vortex)

variables.name: dh
variables.desc: free-surface rise at radius R above the centre (paraboloid)

variables.name: p
variables.desc: pressure at radius r, height z

variables.name: p0
variables.desc: pressure at the free-surface apex (r = 0, z = 0)

variables.name: z
variables.desc: vertical position of the point (up positive, apex z = 0)

assumptions: Steady solid-body rotation about the vertical axis; the free surface is a paraboloid z = ω²r²/(2g). ω is angular (enter rad/s, rpm or rps).
method_references: Solid-body rotation: p = p₀ + ρω²r²/2 − ρgz

fluid_statics.fluid_state_lookup.title: Fluid properties at a state point (CoolProp via common.fluid_state)
assumptions: State defined by temperature and pressure through the shared common.fluid_state adapter (CoolProp real-fluid model). Two-phase states where transport properties are undefined raise an error; give T and P for a single-phase state.

source.derivation: Inclined rectangular gate 2 m wide × 3 m tall along the plane (A = 6 m², centroidal I_c = b·a³/12 = 2·3³/12 = 4.5 m⁴) with centroid depth h_c = 3 m at θ = 30°. F = ρg h_c A = 1000·9.80665·3·6 = 176519.7 N; y_c = h_c/sin30° = 3/0.5 = 6 m; y_cp = y_c + I_c/(A·y_c) = 6 + 4.5/(6·6) = 6 + 0.125 = 6.125 m
F_B = ρgV = 1000·9.80665·0.01 = 98.0665 N (10 L of water displaced)

cases.classification: backend regression; not independent physical validation

source.ref: Water at 20 °C / 1 atm: density 998.2 kg/m³ and dynamic viscosity 1.002 mPa·s (standard textbook values; recalled, not re-read). CoolProp returns 998.21 kg/m³ and 1.0016 mPa·s, within the stated tolerance.
